thread:
Shelly: Heads up — after the maintenance window in eu-west-1 private VPCs we started seeing a small spike of GPU failing health checks. Hosts are reporting driver/module mismatches and some NCCL ring errors.

oncall-bot: [deploy] kernel-updates/eu-west-1 applied to 24 hosts at 2026-03-17T02:12:08Z

Raj: Can you paste a sample error from one of the nodes? if it's driver vs kernel ABI we should detect the exact mismatch.

Shelly: Sure — sample from host private-gpu-32: 
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus
nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol nvidia_pci_probe
NCCL WARN Call to cudaGetDeviceCount failed: startup error
```
Also `nvidia-smi` shows driver 470.141.03 but `modinfo nvidia` shows symbols built for 510.x.

Marta: That looks like a mixed-install. Did the kernel package come from the cloud-image or was it a customer custom kernel? I remember a few private installs using a vendor kernel that rebased to 6.x during the window.

Kevin: On some Private fleets customers install a packaged driver bundle (we call it cust-driver-bundle) that pins to CUDA 11.8 / driver 470. If the kernel got updated to a 6.x ABI, vendor-provided prebuilt modules for 470 will fail. Suggest checking `uname -r` vs `modinfo -F vermagic nvidia` and grep NVML ABI.

Raj: Quick commands to probe — run on one affected host and paste output: 
```
uname -r && modinfo -F vermagic nvidia || true
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv
strings /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/drivers/video/nvidia.ko | grep -Ei "nvml|abi|cuda" | head -n 5
```

Shelly: Ran those on private-gpu-32 and attached logs. vermagic: `6.2.0-rcN SMP mod_unload` but module was built for `5.15.*` so mismatch. Also found `NVML ABI: 2.0` vs expected 3.1 for the runtime.

Marta: OK that confirms a kernel ABI drift from the customer's side (they auto-updated kernel packages during our patch). This is tricky because in Private mode we can't force-replace their driver without consent.

Kevin: Options: 1) advise customer to reboot into previous kernel or install matching driver, 2) provide a compatibility shim (rebuild module on their kernel and provide .ko), or 3) temporarily route inference traffic to Dedicated/hosted for their tenant while they reconcile. Each has operational and legal implications.

Shelly: Customer impact: 9 hosts degraded, 2 hosts totally OOM/NCCL ring failures causing job failures. Traffic drop is approx 12% for that region for this tenant.

Raj: From infra side I can prepare a quick rebuild script that runs DKMS against their kernel and produces a signed module if they want us to help. Need opt-in. I can also add a preflight to Private rollout to detect vendor kernels and warn before kernel pushes.

Marta: Please do the preflight change — we should detect vendor-kernel + cust-driver-bundle combos and block auto-updates or at least flag ops. File an RFC/PR for the preflight check.

Shelly: Filing a support ticket to the customer now, asking them to pause kernel updates and to approve our rebuild assistance. Also reaching out to Legal on scope.

Kevin: Can we add a short-term routing policy: if node fails NVML ABI check, automatically drain and mark as isolation-fallback so the tenant's traffic goes to other capacity (Dedicated/hosted) if available? That would reduce customer-visible errors.

Raj: Yes — I can add an isolation-fallback tag and routing rule, but need a quick SLO exception for the tenant to avoid alerts.

Marta: Action items:
- Raj: build DKMS rebuild script + runbook (ETA 4h)
- Shelly: update customer ticket and ask to pause kernel rollouts (ETA 30m)
- Kevin: implement isolation-fallback rule and SLO mute (ETA 2h)
- Marta: PR for preflight vendor-kernel detection (ETA EOD)

Shelly: tagging @Support to keep them in the loop. We should also add a short confluence note about "Private: kernel-driver coupling risks" so private ops know to ask about kernel auto-updates during onboarding.

oncall-bot: Incident flagged: private-vpc-eu-west1-driver-compat (severity: low-medium) — assigned to Shelly, Raj.

Raj: I'll start on the rebuild script and post progress in this thread. If anyone finds more affected tenants ping me directly. :eyes:

Kevin: thumbs-up.

Shelly: closing loop tomorrow unless customer asks for immediate rebuild. Thanks all.
